comment: Release conditions for every exact-pinned version in package.json (dependencies, devDependencies and
overrides), plus every override added to clear an npm audit advisory reached only transitively.
An exact pin is invisible to a caret-range dependency sweep, so nothing would ever remind you
that a pin is stale. This file is what makes that check happen: run each `check` and compare its trimmed
stdout to `expect`. Equal means the pin is still required; different means the condition that justified it
has changed and the pin should be re-examined. `check: null` means no mechanical test exists - follow
`manualCheck` instead. Every exact pin belongs here, and every entry must name a package that is actually
Known and NOT overridden (2026-10-21): GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm, braces stack exhaustion on deeply nested patterns. It
affects every braces release (<= 3.0.3, no patched version), reached only through markdownlint-cli2 -> micromatch
and globby -> fast-glob, and `npm audit fix --force` would only downgrade markdownlint-cli2 to 0.21.0. Exposure:
braces only expands the glob patterns this repo's own lint:md script and config hand it, never untrusted input,
and it never ships. Add a braces override once a patched release exists.

@codemirror/state.why: obsidian peers on this exact version. Anything else fails npm install with ERESOLVE, and a second copy in the tree breaks editor extensions at runtime.

@codemirror/view.why: obsidian peers on this exact version. Anything else fails npm install with ERESOLVE, and a second copy in the tree breaks editor extensions at runtime.

typescript.why: TypeScript 7 (tsgo) breaks this toolchain: typescript-eslint's parser crashes on the native API, so type-aware ESLint cannot run on 7. typescript-eslint peer-requires the range below, so 6.x is the last usable major.

@puppeteer/browsers.manualCheck: The check reads @wdio/utils's own declared range, not a version, because that range is what makes the override necessary. When it moves to ^3 or later, @wdio/utils no longer pulls extract-zip in and both this override and this entry can go.
@puppeteer/browsers.why: Clears GHSA-jmr9-qjv8-65gv (extract-zip unvalidated symlink path traversal). extract-zip is vulnerable at every published version, so there is nothing to override it to, and the direct dependency cannot be bumped either: even the newest webdriverio reaches extract-zip through @wdio/utils -> @puppeteer/browsers ^2.x. @puppeteer/browsers@3 replaced extract-zip with modern-tar, so forcing 3.x on @wdio/utils, the only consumer left on 2.x, removes the subtree. @wdio/utils imports only install, canDownload, resolveBuildId, detectBrowserPlatform, Browser, ChromeReleaseChannel, computeExecutablePath and the InstallOptions type, all still exported by 3.x, and both packages are ESM-only. Never take the `npm audit fix --force` remedy: it downgrades obsidian-integration-testing to 1.1.2.

deepmerge-ts.manualCheck: The check reads the range declared by the @wdio/utils that obsidian-integration-testing reaches, nested under it when the project also has a newer wdio, which is what forces the override. When it moves to ^8 or later the override and this entry can go. Before lifting it, re-run the deepmergeCustom probe: @wdio/config passes a `mergeArrays` handler that reads `meta.key`, and that is the API 8.0.0 renamed.
deepmerge-ts.why: Clears GHSA-ggr8-5vv4-36mx (stack exhaustion merging recursive object graphs), patched in 8.0.0. @wdio/utils declares ^7.0.3 up to 9.30, and obsidian-integration-testing pins webdriverio 9.27.0, so no direct bump reaches it and `npm audit fix --force` only offers a downgrade of obsidian-integration-testing to 1.1.2. The forced major is safe for these consumers: 8.0.0 breaks by renaming the mergeInfo system and aligning the customization shorthand, and both surfaces were measured to behave identically on 7.1.6 and 8.0.1 in the exact shapes the tree uses -- @wdio/config's `deepmergeCustom` with a `mergeArrays` handler reading `meta.key` and returning `utils.actions.defaultMerge`, and webdriver's `deepmergeCustom({ mergeArrays: false })`. A scan of the whole installed tree found no other binding than `deepmerge` and `deepmergeCustom`.

katex.why: Clears GHSA-238p-pmpm-9mq7 (KaTeX prototype pollution bypassing trust restrictions, >=0.11.0 <0.18.2), which also carried the advisories on micromark-extension-math and markdownlint. Reached only through the toolkit packages -> markdownlint -> micromark-extension-math@3.1.0 (its newest release), which declares katex ^0.16.0, so no bump reaches the fix. The 0.x minor jump is safe because nothing here ever runs KaTeX: markdownlint imports only `math` (the micromark syntax extension) from micromark-extension-math, and katex is required solely by its `mathHtml` half, which markdownlint never loads. NEVER take the `npm audit fix --force` remedy: it downgrades the toolkit packages. Mirrors the same override in obsidian-file-bundles.
katex.manualCheck: The check reads the range micromark-extension-math declares. When it admits 0.18.2 or later the override and this entry can both go.

moment.why: Clears GHSA-4p3w-j4w9-5jqw (moment path traversal via a crafted non-string locale name, >=2.29.2 <2.31.0), which also carried the advisories on obsidian 1.12.3, eslint-plugin-obsidianmd and @mnaoumov/obsidian-dev-toolkit. Reached through eslint-plugin-obsidianmd -> obsidian@1.12.3, which pins moment at the exact 2.29.4. The direct obsidian@1.14.4 already uses 2.31.0, so the override collapses the tree onto that one copy rather than adding a version; it is a minor move within 2.x. Mirrors the same override in obsidian-file-bundles.
moment.manualCheck: The check reads the exact moment pin of the obsidian copy eslint-plugin-obsidianmd brings (it declares obsidian 1.12.3 exactly). When eslint-plugin-obsidianmd moves to an obsidian whose moment is 2.31.0 or later, or that nested copy disappears and the check fails to read it, re-run `npm audit` without the override and drop both if it stays clean.
